evidence_quotes.agenda: Never asked directly, but customer volunteered real concerns unprompted: 'are they gonna go slow on purpose to make money... I just wanna make sure that things are actually being done on time' and 'I'm very pregnant right now so that's why I could use the help.'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Each concern got one direct answer and no second-layer follow-up — e.g. the slow-movers worry got only 'our movers are our direct employees... not contractors' with no 'what else worries you about that' dig.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: 'the more everything is ready, the less you're gonna be paying for at the end of the move' matches the self-prep tip; none of the other four Sheet 5 lines (rate-commit, window framing, beats-it-pay-less, does-that-feel-fair) were said.

top_strength: Handled a genuinely anxious, pregnant customer's unprompted concerns with warmth and patience across a long, detail-heavy call, and adjusted the estimate live when she pushed back on the hour range.
coaching_note: Customer raised two real concerns (slow-move worry, needing physical help) on her own but got single-pass answers instead of a real second layer — ask the agenda question up front so these surface earlier, then dig deeper before pivoting.
